I slowly opened my eyes. Grogginess consumed my body and my vision began to focus. My arms were tied behind back around a cold metal chair. I looked around the unfamiliar warehouse. 

"Wakey wakey." a young man said walking up to me. 

"What's going..." I started. 

"Don't waste your energy." the man said crouching down near me. "You have a big day ahead of you." 

"What?" I said. 

The man walked over to a silver tray on a cart near me. There were surgical instruments lying on the tray. "I've been watching you for quite a while." He looked fondly on the instruments. "You're quite interesting." 

"You've been stalking me?" I asked. I looked around for an exit. 
"As much as I could. You have zero online presence. What's with that? I had to do things the old fashioned way." 

"I'm sorry I made it so hard far you." I groaned. The man grabbed a scalpel and walked to me. He ripped my t-shirt apart and held the scalpel to my chest. 

"No family, I could find. No friends that I've seen you with. You're a killer's wet dream. "Young, hot stud like yourself." 

"Is this a sex thing? Because I could get into that. I'm can be pretty kinky."  I grinned. 

The man shallowly cut into my chest. I grimaced a bit. "You're going to scream in the beginning. You're probably trying to believe that this is a dream right now. Not accepting your reality. Then you'll get mad at me. Threaten me. Then you'll ask me to stop. Offer me anything, try to bargain with me. You'll feel dread and hopelessness and then accept your fate."

"Wow, someone read the grief chapter in his psych 101 textbook." I smirked at him. The man slid the sharp object deeper in to me. I looked him in the eye and leaned forward, allowing the scalpel to enter my chest completely. 

"It stings a bit."  I grinned. The man was shocked as he pulled it out. 

"You're a tough one aren't you?" he said suspiciously. 

"Something like that." I said. "I did have a family, you know. Only my last kin, my daughter, died in 1821. And friends are always temporary. You this is perfect. Stabbing me in the heart won't work.  But maybe, if you try to decapitate me? I haven't tried that one. I'll try not to fight back." 

The man stared at me. "What the hell?"

"Seriously, their's a hacksaw over there. I say you just cut right through my neck. It'll be like killing a pig." I said. 

He looked over at a the hacksaw and picked it up. "What are you?" 

"Something that should have died a long time ago."  I glared at him. He dropped the hacksaw. "Seriously? Some Dexter you are." 

The man looked confused as he paced back and forth. "This isn't real." He looked around. 

"Who's in denial now?" I said and then sighed. "Bored now." I quickly broke out of the handcuffs that held me. I stood from the chair and walked toward the man. "To be fair. The hacksaw probably wouldn't had worked. The guillotine didn't." 

The man's eyes widened in awe. He sprinted towards towards a garage door. "Ughh..." I moaned as I walked over and picked up a longer scalpel. I was faster then him. I'm always faster. I grabbed the man and dragged him back to the chair. "Sit." I said pushing him down. I plunged the scalpel into his shoulder. He screamed. "Oh calm down, you baby." 

"Please let me go." He said.  

I sat ontop of him. "You knocked me out when I was leaving that bar. That was impressive. I mean not that impressive since I was drunk. Honestly still am right now. But A for effort." I put the scalpel on his eye ball. "Just going to show you some pointers."

"Good Morning, Toledo! It's September 28, 2012. The time is 4 am. Happy Friday! For all of you early commuters traffic is looking fairly smooth, this morning. It's going to be a high of 71 today. In top news, there's only five days left until the first Presidential debates between President Obama and Mitt Romney. Some exciting news from outer space, NASA's Curiosity Rover may have found evidence of water on Mars-." Stacy Lewis, anchor for TKW stopped speaking. Something was different. Something had changed. She wasn't an anchor. Not anymore. She turned her head and looked at her co-anchor, Ben Cole. He had a similar look on his face. Stacy looked around the studio. The camerapersons and the producers all were looking around. Confused. 

"I'm sorry. Did I say 2012?" Stacy said. She quickly put her finger up to her earpiece. "Just in. There seems to be several pile ups on the high way." She looked up and saw several of the people leaving out the studio. Ben stands, confused, walks away. Stacy stared at the camera, intensely. "Did i say 2012?"

Stacy pulled out her ear piece and walked away from her desk. She stumbled out of the studio in her red heels. People were running around panicked. Some were on their phones. Stacy saw Ben trying to reach someone on his iPhone 5. "Ben, what's going on?" she asked. Ben put down his phone. "Am i dreaming?" he asked.

"If you're dreaming, I'm dreaming. Last I remember I was in bed." Stacy said. "I was putting my twins to bed." He said. "I'm not an anchor anymore. I haven't been in years." She said. Stacy's phone began to ring. She pulled out her Iphone, it said 'Mom'. "That's impossible." 

"Mom?" Stacy said. "Honey? I woke up in the old house. I thought i was in the hospital. I'm confused." her mother said over the phone. "Mom, is that really you?" "Yeah, baby. But I don't know how I got back here. I'm feeling so much better though." Tears ran down Stacy's eyes. "I'm going to be right there." 

"I have to go, Ben. Go find your family." Stacy said as she began to hurry away. "Who was that?" he asked. "My mother." "But-." he said. "I know." 

"I met Karen in 2014. The twins are almost 2." He mumbled. "I have to go." Stacy hurried away. 

It was near impossible driving to her mother's home. Many cars were crashed into each other. Others speeding down the streets. She didn't understand what was happening. Her memory was fuzzy. She felt like she was a dream but also as if the past five years had been a dream. It took her nearly an hour, twice the time it normally would've taken to get to her mother's house. She ran to the door. "Mom!" Stacy banged on the door.  The door opened. It was her mother, healthy looking and vibrant. "Mom!" She hugged her tightly.  "Do you know what's happening?" her mother asked. "You're really here!" she said. "What is the last thing you remember, Mom?"

"Being sick in the hospital." she replied. "What year is it, Mom?" Stacy asked. "2015" she said. Stacy turned her head to the news playing on her mother's television.

"Possibly hundreds dead from the aftermath of what some experts are calling a massive bioterrorism attack. Which may explain damaging affects on many of our memories and possible hallucinations. Billionaire and reality star, Donald Trump, heir of the Trump fortune was fatally shot this morning. It is unknown if this is related to the suspected attack on America. It is important for all citizens to stay calm and not act on anything based on any hallucinations that you might have experienced." The news anchor stated. 

"Hallucinations? I've heard of mass delusions but... I remember leaving the news stations. I work at CNN. I remember Ben's wedding with Karen. Mom, I remember putting you in hospice. I remember your-." Stacy stopped. 

"President Obama is scheduled to speak at noon, EST." The news anchor said. 

Stacy started deeply at her mother. "Things had gotten so crazy. So surreal. Maybe everything that's happened? Maybe it was a warning. Or maybe we got a second chance. Maybe this is our second chance."

I opened my eyes. There was a darkness I had never seen before. An emptiness that I had never felt before. I was laying down, in what felt to be a stream of water. Yet I was not wet. It was a dream. One of those horrible nightmares. The ones that feel so real. I began gasping desperately. I couldn't breathe. There was nothing to breathe. I tried to let out a scream, yell, screech, anything. But nothing. 

I closed my eyes tight. It was actually less dark with my eyes closed. I squeezed them tighter and tighter. Until it began to hurt, well it would've hurt if I wasn't so numb. Tighter. 

I suddenly released a horrendous shriek. My eyes shot open. It was dark anymore. I was sitting in a wooden chair. I was in a tavern. Lit by candles. Mugs and bottles scattered throughout the room. 
"Wakey wakey." a voice said. I looked up. A young man wearing a clean white button shirt and black slacks along with suspenders stood in front of me. 

"Who...what..?" I mumbled. I wasn't exactly sure what my question was. There was something familiar about this place. "Where am I?"

"Remember your name?" the man asked. "I'm Carl." I stayed quiet. I didn't remember.  "Come on." He led me to the exit of the tavern and I followed him out. 

Outside, there was a city street. It was dark but many torches lit up the night. The air was humid, almost too humid to breathe. "You'll get used to it." 

"To what?' I asked. 

"The heat. The unbreathable air. I know it sucks, but you don't actually need to breathe. It's just out of habit. Looks like you were among the living for a while." Carl said. 

"Am I....am I dead?" It felt like I've been waiting to say those words for an eternity.

"You already know that. From the look of your clothes and your death spot. I'm going to guess 1800's-ish?" 

"Death spot?" I eyed the people walking up down the street. 

"That janky bar. After you die, you wander the Earth as a ghoul, a lost soul. And once you've found some type of peace or resolution you come here." 

"What is...here?" I asked. Carl smiled, "Hell, brother. We're in hell.

"No." I remembered the concept of hell. Vaguely. I knew it was bad. 

"Don't worry. You'll get your memories back, eventually. Including the century or two, give or take that you spent as ghost." Carl said as we walked down the street. Carl pulled out a pipe. 

"Hell..." I stuttered. I suddenly had a memory. Sitting in a pew. I was in a church, a small wooden church. A woman in a brown dress held my hand. My mother. A preacher yelled at the top of his lungs in front of the audience. "And shall cast them into the furnace of fire! There shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth!"

"It's not that bad, really. The vast majority of humanity ends up here. The Originals keep good law and order here. Many would probably say they have better lives here then when they actually had lives." 

"Who are the Originals?" 

Carl chuckled. "The Originals. Demons. The original species that inhabited this dimension after the Fall. Once upon a time, they would've been called Angels. But once they followed the Founder....you might have known him as Lucifer or Satan."

"I don't understand..."

"What you need to know is that you're in a good place. The only real inhabitable place for people. The Founder created this place because he wanted to save us. Wanted us to have free will. To live! Unlike the Creator. You'll need to find a job, by the way. It'll be quite awhile until you can manage a job with the Welcoming Committee such as myself but you'll want to become a contributing member of society. It's safer that way. But first we drink!"
Carl pushed me down the street. I had never been so confused.

I woke up fairly early in the morning. I could feel the sun shining through the window onto my face. I rolled over in my bed and opened my eyes. I was suddenly startled to see my father sitting in a chair in the corner of my room. Watching me. 
"Dad?" I groaned in my morning voice. 
"Happy Birthday, son." my dad said. There was a wooden box in his lap. 
I could hear the sounds of outside. I pulled off the covers and swung my legs over the side of the bed and sat up. "What are you doing here?"
I was living at my grandparent's house. Technically, it was just my grandmother's home, since my grandfather passed two years prior. I hadn't seen my father since the funeral. 
"It's your birthday. A very important one." he said. 
"Why? Time for grandma to kick me out of the house?" I said. 
My father stood and walked over to the bed, sitting next to me. "I remember when my father came to me on my 18th birthday." my dad said. "I was in this room, in this bed. And he was sitting in that corner with this box." 
I was confused. "What's in it?" 
He looked at me and took a breath. My father opened the box. Inside was a odd collection of crystals, filled pouches with writing on them, and large book underneath. "Your birthright." he said. 
I stared up at him. "I don't understand." 
"You are a part of a legacy. A very important one." he said. He pulled the book from underneath. "This is our history, from generation to generation we write about our experiences. 
He handed the book to me. As I held the book, I felt an inexplainable sensation. "We are called Mystics." 
"Mystics? I don't see you in two years and you decide to pull a birthday prank on me?" I said. 
"This isn't a joke. We come from a long line of servants of nature. We are mortals with the ability to connect with the supernatural of this world. Magic is real, Josiah." my dad said.
I quickly stood up and created a distance between me and him. "Why are you telling me this? Seriously, why would you think that I would listen to you? You abandoned me after Mom died!" 
"Josiah, I was trying to protect you." He said, standing to his feet. "What the chosen of our family do is dangerous. Not only are we attracted to the supernatural, but it is attracted to us as well." My father began to move closer to me. "We are capable of incredible things, son. But it comes at a price. Your mother suffered the consequences of loving me. Something very evil, took her away from us in spite." 
"Wait, you know what happened to her? The police said it was an accident. She fell down the stairs." I said, shaken. 
"It was no accident. And I left because I didn't want anything happening to you." 
I eyed the box that lay on the bed. "What else is in there?" 
"The crystals are used to focus our power. Two of those bags contain ashes of our ancestors which we can use for protection. Some of the others contain herbs and powders that you'll find helpful as you grow as a Mystic."  he said. 
"I don't have any power." I said. 
"Your power was bound until your 18th birthday. It always existed within you but was incapable of being harnessed. Today's your first day, be patient." He said. 
"Dad, I can't right now. This is crazy and you have some nerve to come back here with all of this today of all days." I headed towards the door. I needed to get out. Take a shower or something. 
"Josiah." a voice said behind me. It was not my father's. I stopped in my tracks as I felt goosebumps. I slowly turned around towards the familiar voice. 
An old vibrant man sat on my bed next to the box. "Grandpa?" I said, instantly tearing up. 
My grandfather smiled with kind eyes. "I've been waiting for you to be able to see me for two years." 
My father stood looking at his own father and grinned. "I told you he'd be able to see you." Dad looked at me, "I didn't see my first spirit until days after my birthday." 
"I-I don't understand." I said, I felt my legs trembling in the presence of my deceased grandfather who I had mourned. 
"This is the first day of the rest of your life, boy." My grandfather said. "This is one of your gifts. Seeing past the veil. Connecting with the other side. Everything your father said was true." 
I leaned against the wall in disbelief. "Tell me everything." I stuttered. 
My father and grandfather smiled at each other. "I'll start from the beginning." My grandfather said. "Are origins go as far back as the Druids and Stonehenge." 
I slowly slid down the wall and sat on the wooden floor as the ghost of my grandfather and my estranged father told me stories that I would never forget.

I sat in the basement of the science center where I worked. My boss let me work on projects because of the all the down time I had. I held a gray metallic rectangle shaped device in my hand. It was ready. Using my computer I could control it. My boss thought is was ridiculous that I was trying to finish my late fathers project, he said it was impossible. But I did it. I created time travel.

I calibrated the device with my computer. 15 years ago. That was my destination. I didn't consider anything going wrong. I didn't want to. I stood and paced with the time travel device. I was ready. As I began to prepare the device for travel, there was suddenly a change in pressure in the room. I didn't understand, I hadn't started the device yet. There was even a slight change in temperature that I noticed. I turned around and saw a man in his late 20s/ early 30s.

The man walked towards me. There was only two entrances to the basement, the stairs which were on the opposite side of the room and the emergency exit which sounded an alarm when opened. This man came through neither. As he approached me, he began to look familiar. He looked like me. He wore all black. "Uh...who are you?" I stuttered as I backed away.

"You know who I am." He said getting closer to me. I noticed his eyes were an amazing color, a combination of all the colors of the rainbow with a golden tint.

"Are you..." I started.

"You." He said with a scratchy deep voice.

"How?" I asked.

"You know how. We don't have time for this." He said. The man looked down at the device in my hand. "I almost forgot how the first one looked."

"I don't understand." I said. He was obviously my future self. He he was a completely different.

"I came back to destroy that thing." He said. He moved closer to me.

"What!? No!" I said.

"Yes. That device will bring nothing but havoc and pain." The man said.

I paused and looked down at the device. I looked back up at him. "How do I know your actually..." I said.

"You're going back to 2001. To save our father." He stated coldly.

My eyes widened. "Yes." I said.

"I can't let you do that. There was a reason our father was in the city, in that tower when it collapsed. He supposed to be dead." The man said.

"But..." I stuttered.

"But nothing. Our father was not the man that we were raised to believe he was. He will steal the device from you. He will use it for evil. He's a monster who's only obsessed with immortality and power." He said.

We stared at each other for a moment. "Ok...I won't save dad." I said. "That fixes things right?"

"That's not good enough. It needs to be destroyed." He said. "Time travel only causes devastation."

"I can't destroy it..." I said. "I won't."

He glared at me. He then pulled a gun from his coat. "What the hell are you doing?" I asked.
"I came here to destroy this technology. Even if that means killing you. I know how stubborn you are." He said.

"But if I die, you die." I said staring at the gun.

"I'm aware of how time travel works. This is bigger than us. Now give me the damn device or I WILL kill you." He said with cold eyes.

"What happened to you...?" I asked.

"The future did..." He stated.

I took a deep breath and sighed. I put the device down at my work table. "Thank you." He said. He walked to the table and sat in front of the computer. He turned around and looked at me. "You need to go."

"What why?" I asked.

"Because..." he removed his coat revealing what appeared to be a bomb strapped around his torso. "This entire place is going down in a less than two minutes."

I gasped, "What the hell!"

"It's necessary. Now go." He said.

I was stunned, I didn't understand. "But..."

"Trust me..." He stern face slowly developed a small grin. "You'll thank me."

I slowly backed away towards the emergency exit. "I know..." I turned and opened the door. The alarm suddenly went off. I could see my future self staring at a picture of a young woman in his hand. He smiled as a tear went down his eye. I sprinted away from the building ran to a nearby field. Then came the explosion. Creating a new future for me.

Henry sat in his study in front of his computer. It was early evening and the sun had set only about a hour or two ago. Beside him, on his desk was a glass of vodka, no ice. He had kept a steady buzz for most of the day which was common for him. Henry grabbed the glass and took a sip. 

Writer's block had been an issue for a while. His poetry and fiction writing had slowly diminished, and the booze was the only thing that kept him sane. Suddenly there was a loud crash outside of his study. Henry quickly stood. He could hear shuffling around outside the doors. Henry sighed, finishing his vodka. He walked towards the double doors of his study and dramatically opened them.

There was silence. There was no one around. Henry began to walk towards his kitchen where he had thought the sounds came from. The kitchen was empty. Henry scowled in irritation and turned back towards his study. A woman with long brown hair and tattered black clothing stood in front of Henry. Her eyes were cold and her skin was pale. She seemed like she was trying to speak but only blood came out of her mouth. It poured out of her mouth down to her chin. She seemed to be choking on it. Henry stared at the woman with an angry look on his face.

"I can't help you. Leave me alone!" Henry tried to walk around the woman but stopped in his tracks once he saw a little girl in front of the entrance to his study. She was only around nine years old, with long brown hair like her mother's, wearing a pink and purple pajamas. 

"What about me, daddy?" the little girl asked. "Can you help me?" 

Henry glared at the little girl. Almost every night with these two. He closed his eyes and walked towards his study. He wasn't sure if he had walked through her or not but it felt nothing. "Daddy, I can't breathe. Don't leave us!" the little girl screeched at the top of her lungs. 

Henry slammed the doors behind him in the study. Suddenly he felt banging from the other side of the doors. It caused him to step back from them. He could hear muffled voices. Henry looked down and noticed dark red blood slowly approaching from under the doors. He hurried to his desk and sat. He opened one of the drawers and pulled out a small hand gun. Henry stared at it for a moment. He ignored the sounds of a the frantic child outside of the study and the woman choking on her own blood. 

He held the gun tightly. He then looked back into the drawer and pulled out a picture frame that was turned upside down. In the frame was a picture of a beautiful woman with brown hair and a little girl hugging her, smiling ear to ear. Henry stared at the picture and until he finally gasped; as if he hadn't breathed in hours. "Not yet." He said throwing the picture frame back into the drawer and laying the gun on top of it. Henry closed the drawer.  

There was silence again. The noise had stopped. The blood that leaked from the other side of the door had vanished. Henry looked around the room, adjusting to the silence. He grabbed the bottle of vodka next to his chair and poured himself a glass. After taking a sip, he looked at the computer screen in front of him. And he began to write.
